data.title: Binance reveals a $1B SpaceX stake: what happens if it sells its stake?
data.description:
SpaceX (SPCX) shares fell roughly 5% in trading Friday as tech stocks fell after Amazon and Intel's disappointing earnings.

Binance’s response to a massive cryptocurrency theft put its investment in Elon Musk’s company in the spotlight.

Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao said the exchange’s SpaceX holdings were worth more than $1 billion, raising questions about whether those shares could become a source of emergency funding.

Fellow co-founder Yi He subsequently said a sale of SpaceX stock was unnecessary.

For investors, the distinction matters: a potential seller has emerged in the conversation, but no disposal has been announced.

Why Binance’s SpaceX stake is suddenly in focus

The discussion followed a hack that drained $6.3 billion from Binance.

After Musk reacted to social-media commentary about the incident, Zhao pointed to Binance’s SpaceX investment while asking him to show support.

Yi He then said the exchange’s annual revenue was sufficient to cover the losses without selling those holdings.

That reassurance addresses the immediate liquidation concern, but it leaves an important financial distinction unresolved.

Revenue is not the same as profit or readily available cash.

Investors assessing the likelihood of a sale would need greater visibility into Binance’s accessible corporate funds, eventual recoveries, and reimbursement obligations.

Equally, customer assets under custody should not be confused with money belonging to the exchange. Their size alone cannot establish Binance’s capacity to absorb losses.

What would happen if Binance sold SPCX shares

A disposal would create additional supply of existing SpaceX shares.

It would not, by itself, dilute shareholders or remove cash from SpaceX’s balance sheet: proceeds would go to the selling investor.

The immediate market impact would depend on execution.

A rapid sale through the market could pressure prices, particularly during thinner trading.

A negotiated placement with institutional buyers could distribute the holding more efficiently, although buyers might demand a discount.

The psychological effect could extend beyond the actual transaction.

Traders anticipating a large seller may reduce exposure before any shares change hands, creating a temporary overhang.

However, neither the stake’s reported value nor Friday’s decline establishes how far SPCX would fall.

Binance has not announced a sale, and Zhao subsequently clarified that he had not proposed one.

A potential selling overhang is not an operating setback

For SpaceX investors, the central question is whether this remains a funding discussion at an outside shareholder or develops into an actual transaction.

A Binance sale motivated by reimbursement needs would reveal more about the seller’s liquidity requirements than SpaceX’s operating outlook.

It would not automatically signal weaker demand, deteriorating margins, or a change in the company’s competitive position.

Still, dismissing the issue entirely would overlook how markets price uncertainty.

Any subsequent announcement specifying sale size, timing, or restrictions could change the assessment.

For now, Yi He’s statement reduces the immediate forced-sale concern.

Friday’s decline is observable; attributing the entire move to Binance would go beyond the available evidence.

Investors should distinguish confirmed selling from speculation before treating this as either a lasting setback or an obvious buying opportunity.

data.title: Gold price crash accelerates as crude oil rises and odds of Fed rate hike jumps
data.description:
Gold price continued its downward trend, reaching its lowest level in months as demand waned after the hawkish Federal Reserve interest rate decision. It dropped to $3,925, down modestly from the August high of $4,700. This sell-off may continue as President Donald Trump prepares to escalate his attacks against Iran.

Gold price technical analysis

The daily chart shows that gold has come under pressure in the past few weeks, moving from a high of $4,700 in September to a low of $3,958. It has now crossed the important support level of $4,000 as it continued its series of lower lows and lower highs.

Gold formed a death cross pattern, which forms when the 50-day moving average crosses the 200-day moving average. This pattern often leads to more downside. At the same time, the Relative Strength Index (RSI) has dropped from the overbought level of 72.5

Therefore, these patterns suggest that gold may continue falling, potentially to the next key support level of $3,900. The risk, however, is that gold has formed a triple-bottom pattern whose neckline is at $4,700. This pattern means that sellers may attempt to push it higher in the near term. 

Gold price chart | Source: TradingView

Gold is falling as crude oil prices rise after FOMC decision

The ongoing gold price rally is happening as crude oil rally continues. Brent, the international benchmark, rose to $113, while the West Texas Intermediate (WTI) moved to $104. Higher oil prices mean that inflation will remain stubbornly high in the foreseeable future. 

Oil prices will likely continue rising after the US midterm elections in which Democrats are expected to win the House of Representatives and the Senate. President Donald Trump has warned that he will launch a short attack on Iran in a bid to put pressure on the IRGC to talk. Iran has warned that it will escalate if the US attacks it. 

The most recent data showed that the headline consumer price index (CPI) rose 3.7% last month, while the core figure moved to 2.7%. Similarly, the headline and core personal consumption expenditure (PCE) remained above the 2% target during the month. 

These numbers mean that the Federal Reserve will likely maintain higher interest rates for longer. In its last decision this week, the bank decided to leave rates unchanged between 3.75% and 4%. Two officials - Beth Hammack and Lisa Cook - voted to hike interest rates.

In his statement after the Fed decision, Governor Kevin Warsh maintained that inflation remained stubbornly high and that the Fed will do whatever it takes to bring it down. As a result, analysts expect the bank to hike interest rates in its December meeting. 

Gold tends to underperform the market when the Fed is hiking interest rates and when bond yields are at an elevated level.

data.title: Vonovia share price slowly forms a risky inverted C&H pattern as risks rise
data.description:
Vonovia share price continued its strong sell-off this week as the company published a surprise report, lowering its guidance for the year. It dropped to a low of €15.25 before paring back some of these losses to the current €16.24. It is now hovering near its lowest level since 2014 after falling by 73% from its highest point in 2022.

Vonovia exposed as Berlin plans house seizure

Vonovia, the biggest landlord in Germany, is facing major challenges. One of these risks is a new law in Berlin that allows authorities to seize houses in a bid to lower prices.

The proposal is for authorities to buy these houses from their current owners and then lower rents that people pay. In this case, the estimate is that the government will spend about €100,000 per apartment, much lower than their current values. 

As a result, Vonovia is expected to lose about €8.4 billion as 120,000 of its apartments are brought into public ownership. Estimates are that the company’s properties are valued at about €130,000.

Still, it is unclear whether this will happen, as Vonovia and other companies in the industry have vowed to sue. The national government, under Friedrich Merz, have also urged against seizing these properties. He argues that it will be illegal and make it hard to attract investors in the real estate sector. 

Vonovia expects its business to weaken

Vonovia shares also dropped after the company published a statement warning about its business as interest rates and financing costs continue rising. The company blamed the crisis to the US-Iran war that led to higher inflation in Germany and other countries.

In the aftermath, interest rates and bond yields have continued rising. The European Central Bank (ECB) hiked interest rates in September and analysts now expect it to deliver more hikes in the coming months. 

As a result, the company’s re-offer yield of its eight-year unsecured bonds jumped by 140 basis points. Its bonds that are maturing in 2032 are yielding 6.71%, much higher than the year-to-date low of 5.2%.

Vonovia’s preliminary nine-month results for the first nine months of the year showed that its adjusted EBITDA will be €2.19 billion, up from €2.118 billion in the same period last year. In the statement, the management said:

“Vonovia remains committed to deleveraging and will continue its disposal program as a matter of top priority. Its deleveraging targets remain unchanged: net debt/EBITDA is expected to improve to below 12x and the interest coverage ratio to remain comfortably above 3x by the end of 2028.”

Vonovia share price technical analysis

Vonovia stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that Vonovia shares have slumped in the past few years, moving from a high of €33.93 in 2024 to the current 16.28. It has slowly formed an inverted cup-and-handle pattern whose lower side is at €15.25. This pattern often leads to more continuation.

The stock has slumped below the 50-week and 100-week Exponential Moving Averages (EMA). Remaining below that level is a sign that investors remain in control. Therefore, the stock will likely continue falling, potentially to the key support level of €13.

data.title: Chevron shares rise after third-quarter profit jumps nearly 200%
data.description:
Chevron Corp. CVX reported stronger-than-expected third-quarter earnings on Friday as disruptions to global fuel supplies lifted refining margins, helping the oil major offset weaker contributions from its oil and gas production business.

The stock was up 1.25% in premarket trading.

The company reported net income of $9.9 billion, or $5.06 per share, compared with $3.5 billion, or $1.82 per share, in the same period last year.

Adjusted earnings, excluding special items and foreign currency effects, came in at $10.4 billion, or $5.28 per share, beating the average analyst estimate of $4.89, according to LSEG data.

Revenue reached approximately $67.8 billion, beating estimates comfortably.

Refining business drives earnings beat

Chevron’s downstream division, which includes refining and fuel sales, generated $4.9 billion in earnings, more than four times the $1.1 billion recorded a year earlier and slightly higher than the previous quarter.

The improvement came as attacks on refining facilities in Russia and the Middle East disrupted fuel production, tightening supplies of diesel and other refined products and pushing margins higher.

Chevron’s US refineries processed a record more than 1 million barrels of crude per day during the quarter, with the facilities running at 98% capacity.

Production yields of diesel and jet fuel also increased by more than 10%, reflecting strong demand for refined products.

The upstream business, which covers oil and gas exploration and production, generated $5.7 billion in earnings.

Although higher than the $3.3 billion reported a year earlier, the figure declined 30% from the second quarter as crude prices eased.

Worldwide production averaged 3.98 million barrels of oil equivalent per day, down 2% from the previous quarter.

The company also recorded its first month of equity-accounted production from Venezuela under improved fiscal terms, with total production costs below $20 per barrel.

However, production in the third quarter of 2026 was lower than a year ago primarily due to lower
entitlements from higher prices and impacts from the Middle East conflict

Cash generation supports shareholder returns

Cash flow from operations reached $16 billion, while adjusted free cash flow climbed to $14.2 billion, twice the level recorded a year earlier.

Chevron distributed $3.5 billion in dividends and repurchased $2.5 billion worth of shares during the quarter.

Net debt declined to $20.7 billion from $34.5 billion at the end of 2025.

Chief Executive Mike Wirth said the company delivered strong operational performance while continuing to invest in expanding energy supplies.

Chevron’s board also declared a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share.

Oil majors benefit from refining boom

Other major energy companies also reported strong third-quarter performances.

ExxonMobil posted adjusted earnings of $17.5 billion, while Shell reported adjusted earnings of $10.8 billion and announced a $5 billion share buyback programme.

BP's third-quarter profit quadrupled to $8.46 billion, its highest on record, as refining margins and energy prices strengthened.

data.title: Top DAX Index shares to watch next week: Bayer, BMW, Rheinmetall, Vonovia
data.description:
The DAX Index wavered as investors reacted to the European Central Bank (ECB) interest rate decision and earnings by top companies like Deutsche Bank, BASF, Mercedes-Benz, Linde, and Adidas. This article looks at some of the top German companies to watch next week.

DAX Index to react to Bayer earnings

Bayer stock has done well in the past few months, soaring by over 50% from its lowest level this year. This rally continued rising after the company won another round of Roundup weedkiller cancer trial. A jury sided with the company in the first trial after the Supreme Court ruled in its favor a few months ago. The company is still waiting for a broader ruling from a separate court on the $7.25 billion effort to settle other Roundup cases.

The most recent results showed that Bayer’s sales rose by 3% in the third quarter to €24.3 billion, with its core EPS rising by 3% to €3.6. Most of its revenue growth was driven by its crop science business, whose revenue rose by 5.5%. Its pharmaceuticals and consumer health revenue rose by 3.5% and 0.2%, respectively. The upcoming earnings report will provide more hints on what to expect.

BMW earnings to shed color on its turnaround

BMW stock has plunged in the past few months as concerns about the European auto industry continued. It was trading at €57.92 on Friday, down by 50% from its all-time high of €115, which it achieved in 2024.

The retreat has coincided with that of other European companies like Volkswagen and Mercedes-Benz. In its earnings this week, Volkswagen posted its biggest loss since the Dieselgate scandal. The management warned that the mounting losses threatened its ability to compete. 

It warned that its margins were too low to continue investing in technologies that are essential to its future. Deliveries to China tumbled by 30% in the last quarter. 

Therefore, BMW stock will react to the upcoming results, which will provide more hints on its business, especially in China. The results will also provide hints on whether its turnaround is continuing. 

Rheinmetall 

Rheinmetall, the biggest defense group in Europe, has been in a strong sell-off in the past few months. It has dropped from €2,005 in September to the current €1,037, making one of last year’s best performers in the DAX index into one of the worst. 

The stock’s retreat continued after Germany cancelled its frigate program that was supposed to earn it billions of dollars. It is also facing supply chain issues because of the ongoing US-Iran war. The war has also led to a surge in raw material costs.

Rheinmetall’s stock retreat has also coincided with that of its American peers like Lockheed Martin and RTX. Its upcoming earnings report will provide more color on its business. 

There are other top DAX Index companies to watch next week. The most notable ones will be Deutsche Telekom, Deutsche Post, Commerzbank, and Siemens Healthineers. Vonovia, a company whose business is under pressure from a new Berlin law, will also release its earnings..

data.title: Foxconn dismisses AI bubble fears with fresh OpenAI partnership on cards
data.description:
Foxconn is preparing to deepen its relationship with OpenAI as the world's largest contract electronics manufacturer looks to expand its role in the rapidly growing AI infrastructure market.

Chairman Young Liu confirmed that a fresh collaboration was in the works after meeting OpenAI CEO Sam Altman on Friday at the company's annual technology event in Taipei.

Liu said further details would be announced once the terms were finalised, without disclosing the scope of the proposed arrangement.

The development builds on an existing partnership between the companies, announced in November 2025, to design and develop next-generation AI data-centre hardware and strengthen US manufacturing capabilities.

Existing partnership provides foundation

Under their earlier agreement, OpenAI agreed to share its infrastructure requirements to help Foxconn design multiple generations of AI data-centre racks.

The collaboration also covered the manufacturing of critical equipment, including networking, cabling, cooling and power systems, at Foxconn's US facilities.

Importantly, the initial agreement did not include purchase commitments or financial obligations. OpenAI was given early access to evaluate the equipment and an option to purchase the systems.

The Nvidia supplier has since expanded its AI server manufacturing operations in the US.

The company operates six factory buildings in Houston, Texas, where it produces AI servers for Nvidia, and Liu said further expansion would be needed.

Its cloud and networking business, which includes AI servers, accounted for 51% of Foxconn's second-quarter revenue, crossing the 50% mark for the first time.

Foxconn pushes back against AI bubble concerns

The potential expansion of its OpenAI relationship comes as investors increasingly question whether the enormous investments in AI infrastructure will generate sufficient returns.

Even top industry executives have acknowledged market risk as spending continues to increase amid rising borrowing costs.

Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang recently said demand for neocloud companies is "off the charts," but a shortage of working capital is limiting growth

Google CEO Sundar Pichai had previously cautioned that "elements of irrationality" exist within current investment valuations.

Technology stocks have faced bouts of selling as concerns grow over rising borrowing costs, infrastructure expenses and the time required to monetise AI investments.

Liu dismissed concerns that the sector is experiencing a bubble, arguing that demand for computing infrastructure remains strong.

He also expects Foxconn to maintain double-digit revenue growth next year, supported by its expanding AI server business.

Humanoid robots enter Texas facilities

Separately, Foxconn is stepping up its automation efforts, with more than 10 humanoid robots already deployed at its Texas facilities for internal use, according to Reuters.

Brand Cheng, chairman of Foxconn subsidiary Foxconn Industrial Internet, told Reuters that the company plans to expand robot deployment beyond Texas.

The subsidiary has introduced two wheeled robot models designed for tasks such as lifting, assembly, and loading and unloading materials.

It is also developing AI models for humanoid robots using Nvidia's GR00T foundation model.

The developments highlight Foxconn's broader push to position itself across the AI ecosystem, from manufacturing the hardware powering AI systems to using robotics in its own production facilities.

data.title: Reddit stock plunges 25% on user growth concerns; analysts turn cautious
data.description:
Reddit shares RDDT plunged more than 25% at market open on Friday after the social media company warned that user growth could weaken further in the fourth quarter as declining traffic from Google search weighs on its audience.

Chief Executive Steve Huffman said daily active unique visitors could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the current quarter from approximately 130 million if referral traffic continues to decline.

The warning overshadowed stronger-than-expected third-quarter results and a 53% increase in revenue.

The company also forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, below the Bloomberg consensus estimate of $1.05 billion, raising concerns about whether its advertising business can maintain its growth momentum amid changes in online search.

The outlook prompted several analysts to reassess the stock, which has fallen 46% this year.

BofA Securities and Citizens downgraded their ratings, while Guggenheim and Needham retained Buy recommendations but substantially reduced their price targets.

Google’s AI search raises traffic concerns

Reddit has increasingly blamed changes to Google's search experience for reducing the number of users directed to its platform.

AI-powered search features can answer queries directly, potentially limiting the need for users to click through to websites and online communities.

Huffman said search engine referrals to Reddit had declined by more than one million on average each week during October.

He also argued that Google's AI search experience was failing to direct users to the platform despite continued crawling of its content.

"Google is crawling us as hard as ever, so the demand hasn't changed from their point of view either. The reality is, the AI mode does not drive traffic, not for us and not to anybody," Huffman said on the post-earnings call.

The company is responding by shifting its focus towards registered users and its mobile application.

On Thursday, Huffman outlined plans to require sign-ins for access to most content, partly to deter data scraping by artificial intelligence companies.

The strategy could help Reddit protect its data and improve advertising targeting, but it also carries the risk of reducing the number of casual visitors who access its communities through search engines.

Reddit's global daily active uniques were flat quarter over quarter at 130.3 million in the third quarter, although they were up 12% from a year earlier.

In the US, daily active uniques fell to 50.7 million from 53.2 million in the second quarter, marking a 2% year-over-year decline.

The US decline is particularly significant because it represents the first annual contraction in the metric since Reddit went public in 2024.

Huffman sought to emphasise that the company's most valuable audience remained intact.

"The vast majority of our revenue comes from our app users and logged-in users are direct traffic, and both of those are up Q. over Q., and so that’s where our focus is," he said.

Reddit generates most of its revenue from online advertising and can monetise registered users more effectively because they tend to be more active and provide advertisers with better opportunities for targeted campaigns.

Strong third-quarter results fail to reassure investors

Reddit reported third-quarter revenue of $895 million, up 53% year over year and above the Bloomberg consensus estimate of $869.6 million.

Net income climbed to $283 million, or $1.40 per diluted share, compared with analyst expectations of $272.6 million.

Adjusted EBITDA increased 70% to $402 million, exceeding the $398.5 million estimate.

However, the latest revenue growth marked a slowdown from the company's previous performance.

Reddit had reported eight consecutive quarters of revenue growth exceeding 60% as recently as its second-quarter results in July.

The weaker growth trajectory, combined with the user figures and fourth-quarter forecast, raised questions about whether the company can sustain its rapid expansion.

Huffman described the revenue outlook as resilient despite the pressure on search traffic.

“It’s still a strong guide,” he said. “We are still growing at an industry-leading rate, and that’s despite the headwinds from search referrals.”

Analysts cut price targets as outlook deteriorates

BofA Securities lowered its price target on Reddit to $135 from $190 while maintaining a Neutral rating.

Reddit stock closed at $129 per share on Thursday.

The firm expects investor sentiment to remain subdued for several quarters until the company establishes a positive trajectory for US logged-in user growth, which has been challenging since 2024.

BofA also warned that traffic headwinds could intensify before improving and highlighted uncertainty surrounding Reddit's planned transition towards a logged-in-only experience.

The firm cited the renewal of the company's Google data licensing agreement in the first quarter of 2027 as another source of uncertainty.

At an after-hours share price of $106, BofA valued Reddit at nine times its estimated 2027 EBITDA and seven times its 2028 EBITDA, broadly in line with peers despite higher revenue growth expectations.

Citizens downgraded Reddit to Market Perform from Market Outperform, citing declining user growth and reduced referrals from Google.

Analyst Andrew Boone noted that US daily active users had fallen 5% quarter over quarter and warned that Google's push towards AI-powered search could worsen the platform's logged-out traffic problems.

Citizens acknowledged that Reddit continued to execute well on monetisation but said uncertainty surrounding user growth was putting greater pressure on its ability to generate revenue from existing users.

The firm believes the shares are now fairly valued.

Guggenheim cut its price target to $170 from $255 while maintaining a Buy rating.

It reduced the valuation multiple applied to its 2027 operating income before depreciation and amortisation estimate to 18 times from 25 times, citing investor concerns over referral traffic and the shift towards registered users.

Needham also retained its Buy rating but lowered its price target sharply to $150 from $300.

The firm said Reddit's focus on logged-in and app users, which accounted for more than 80% of third-quarter revenue, could reduce customer churn, improve advertising targeting and protect company data from large language models.

Needham said one negative interpretation of management's commentary was that Reddit might not renew its Gemini large language model deal.

However, it argued that platforms with more restricted access to their audiences could ultimately monetise users more effectively than companies dependent on the open internet.

The diverging analyst views reflect the central question facing Reddit: whether its strategy of prioritising registered users can offset the loss of search-driven visitors without undermining the audience growth that has supported its advertising business.

data.title: Nasdaq opens 2% lower as Amazon and Intel selloff deepens AI spending concerns
data.description:
US stocks opened lower on Friday as disappointing results from Amazon and a weak outlook from Intel intensified concerns about the rising costs of artificial intelligence infrastructure and the time required for companies to generate returns on their investments.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.44%, while the S&P 500 dropped 1.3%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 175 points.

Friday was the final trading session of October, with the Nasdaq Composite on track to end the month lower despite gains in the broader market.

Amazon and Intel lead technology sell-off

Amazon shares fell around 4.4% in trading after the company reported third-quarter revenue and earnings below Wall Street expectations.

The e-commerce and cloud computing giant also reported negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion over the trailing 12 months, compared with positive cash flow of $14.8 billion in the year-earlier period.

Amazon maintained its capital expenditure forecast of approximately $220 billion for 2026, adding to concerns about the scale of its AI infrastructure investments and the pressure on cash generation.

Intel shares plunged more than 29% after the chipmaker issued a weaker-than-expected outlook for the current quarter.

The company faces challenges from a slowing personal computer market, manufacturing bottlenecks, and heavy investment to expand production capacity.

Intel's client computing revenue declined 5% year over year to $8.1 billion in the third quarter, reflecting pressure in the PC market.

Other semiconductor and hardware stocks also fell.

Advanced Micro Devices dropped 9%, Nvidia declined 3.3%, and server makers Dell and HP lost 8.3% and 5.6%, respectively. SanDisk shares fell 7% despite quarterly results that exceeded estimates.

AI investment costs weigh on market sentiment

The sell-off reflects growing scrutiny of the spending required to build AI data centres and expand computing capacity.

Investors are increasingly assessing whether the expected returns from these investments will justify the substantial capital commitments.

Alphabet shares slipped around 1% in trading after plunging 12% on Thursday.

The Google parent reported disappointing results in its search advertising business and negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion in the third quarter.

Meta also reported cash outflows during the September quarter, while Microsoft delivered a stronger-than-expected cash flow result despite raising $25 billion through a bond sale.

Concerns have also spread to companies providing AI infrastructure.

CoreWeave shares have fallen around 36% in October, while Nebius is heading for a monthly decline of approximately 32%, as investors assess debt levels and financing costs across the sector.

Meanwhile, Procter & Gamble, Walmart and Coca-Cola gained around 2% in trading, alongside healthcare stocks.

Nasdaq heads for monthly decline

Despite the latest losses, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq were still on course for weekly gains, following a brief recovery in technology stocks earlier in the week after Anthropic unveiled its US initial public offering filing.

However, the Nasdaq Composite was heading for a decline of approximately 2.5% for October, potentially ending its two-month winning streak.

The S&P 500 was on track to gain 0.9%, while the Dow was set to rise 2.8%.

Nine of the 11 S&P 500 sectors were expected to record monthly gains.

Technology and communication services were among the exceptions, with communication services heading for its worst month since April 2022.

Investors were also monitoring interest-rate expectations.

Markets were pricing in more than 50 basis points of Federal Reserve rate increases by mid-2027, according to LSEG data, despite the central bank holding rates steady earlier in the week.

data.title: CXMT posts 613% jump in revenue as Micron, SanDisk shares tumble
data.description:
China’s ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) reported a more than sevenfold increase in third-quarter revenue on Friday, benefiting from a never-ending demand for memory chips used in artificial intelligence infrastructure amid a squeeze in global supplies.

The results underline the Chinese chipmaker’s growing position in the global memory industry, where established players such as Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron are facing a more competitive landscape.

The earnings announcement came as US memory and storage stocks also faced pressure ahead of the opening bell.

CXMT revenue jumps 613%

CXMT reported net profit attributable to shareholders of 54.4 billion yuan ($8.17 billion) for the three months ended September 30, reversing a loss in the same period last year.

Revenue climbed 613.2% year over year to 118.71 billion yuan ($16.7 billion), representing a 19.3% increase from the previous quarter.

However, the sequential increase in attributable profit was much more modest, at around 3%.

For the first nine months of 2026, revenue reached 269.02 billion yuan, while net profit attributable to shareholders stood at 132.04 billion yuan.

The company had recorded a loss of about 5.3 billion yuan in the corresponding period last year.

CXMT attributed the improvement to higher memory-chip prices amid tight supply, alongside capacity expansion and a shift towards a more favourable product mix.

As major rivals increasingly prioritise higher-value products such as high-bandwidth memory (HBM), CXMT has benefited from demand for conventional DRAM products.

CXMT shares retreat after blockbuster debut

CXMT made its Shanghai stock market debut in July, with shares surging 466% on their first trading day and briefly making it China's most valuable listed company.

Its 58-billion-yuan offering was Asia's largest IPO this year.

However, the stock has since lost ground, closing 2.5% lower on Friday. It has fallen approximately 32% from its August peak as investors reassess valuations and the sustainability of the AI investment boom.

US memory stocks also came under pressure in premarket trading, with Micron dropping over 6% and SanDisk down close to 9.5%. In South Korea, Samsung fell 3% while SK Hynix tumbled to close 7% lower.

Investors are weighing the durability of elevated memory margins against the possibility of additional competition and the overall sustainability of the AI trade.

New technology adds to competitive concerns

CXMT had also reported progress on a new DRAM cell architecture known as 4F², designed to fit more memory cells onto a chip and potentially increase storage density.

The company plans to introduce a server-memory product using the technology by the end of 2026.

Samsung and SK Hynix are pursuing similar approaches, making the technology an important area of competition among memory manufacturers.

Earlier reports of CXMT’s progress triggered a selloff across global chip stocks as investors assessed the potential impact on established suppliers.

The technology has yet to demonstrate large-scale commercial production, but CXMT’s rapid financial growth and manufacturing expansion are already adding to pressure on established memory-chip makers.

data.title: Is Intel stock a buy after its 26% post-earnings fall? Here's what analysts say
data.description:
Intel shares INTC plunged about 26% in premarket trading on Friday after the chipmaker issued a weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter revenue forecast, citing continued weakness in the global personal computer market and manufacturing constraints.

The decline followed the company's third-quarter earnings report, which showed adjusted earnings per share of 52 cents, beating analysts' expectations of 40 cents.

Revenue came in at $16.51 billion, slightly above the $16.5 billion consensus estimate.

However, investors focused on the outlook for the December quarter.

Intel expects revenue of between $15 billion and $16 billion, well below the $17.1 billion forecast by analysts tracked by FactSet.

The company also expects PC chip revenue to decline in the mid-20% range in the fourth quarter, following a 5% drop to $8.10 billion in the September quarter.

If the premarket losses hold, Intel would record its biggest one-day share-price decline in more than two years.

The company is also on track to lose more than $100 billion in market capitalisation, which would represent its largest single-day market value decline on record, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

Intel finance chief David Zinsner said the weakness in the PC market was expected to persist into next year.

“We see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year,” Zinsner said in the earnings release.

“We will continue making disciplined investments in capacity and working capital to increase supply and support future growth.”

Manufacturing disruptions add to PC market weakness

Intel's forecast also reflects the impact of an explosion at a fabrication plant in Israel earlier this month that killed two workers and seriously injured a third.

The incident is expected to cost the company about $600 million in lost revenue over two quarters, Zinsner said during Thursday's earnings call.

Chief executive Lip-Bu Tan described the incident as an “unfortunate and tragic accident” that caused an “extended shutdown” at the facility, affecting shipments of 10-nanometre chips.

The company is facing additional pressure from rising memory-chip prices, which have made PCs more expensive, while tighter information technology budgets are also weighing on demand.

Like other major technology companies, Intel has been investing heavily in manufacturing capacity.

However, supply disruptions have limited its ability to capitalise on demand for data-centre chips.

"I'm disappointed that we were not able to meet strong customer demand in this quarter," Tan said on a conference call with analysts.

"We face near-term challenges, ​including manufacturing supply shortages, the unprecedented memory crunch, and the resulting softness in PC demand."

Analysts cut price targets as market-share concerns grow

The weak outlook prompted several analysts to reassess their expectations for Intel, with concerns extending beyond the near-term PC market slowdown to its competitive position in processors and foundry services.

BofA Securities downgraded Intel to Neutral from Buy and cut its price target to $100 from $145.

The firm said Intel had not demonstrated sufficient progress in attracting external foundry customers.

It expects PC shipments to decline 25% to 30% quarter-on-quarter in the fourth quarter, with further inventory correction likely during the first half of 2027.

BofA noted that Intel's data-centre CPU business was performing well amid rising demand for agentic applications, but supply constraints related to substrates were limiting growth.

It also said Intel's products were not yet technically competitive with AMD and ARM-based rivals, which were growing two to four times faster.

The firm acknowledged Intel's longer-term potential to build a competitive domestic foundry operation, adding that evidence of progress could support a recovery in the stock.

However, near-term weakness in PC and foundry operations was offsetting strength in data-centre demand.

Roth Capital analyst Suji Desilva also downgraded Intel to Neutral from Buy and slashed the price target to $70 from $120.

Morgan Stanley analysts led by Joseph Moore said Intel's stock remained unattractive even after the steep decline.

They expect the company to lose market share to fabless competitors with lower capital spending requirements.

Advanced Micro Devices, Nvidia, Graviton and Axion are expected to materially outgrow Intel's 30% market growth rate in CPUs in 2027.

Jefferies analysts led by Blayne Curtis, meanwhile, viewed the revenue reset as less concerning because it was driven by weaker PC demand rather than a deterioration in the data-centre and AI business.

However, they warned that Intel could continue losing market share next year, "making it tough to underwrite the longer-term story even with Foundry/packaging customer announcements."

AI business offers a longer-term counterpoint

Despite the negative outlook, some investors see Intel's expanding data-centre business and foundry ambitions as potential drivers of a longer-term recovery.

Nicholas Mugalli of World Trade Securities said the company's AI business was growing while its traditional PC operations were contracting.

"The AI side of Intel is booming, and the old PC side is shrinking. For now the old side is bigger, so it wins the guide. Note too that $0.17 of this quarter's EPS came from a mark-to-market gain, not the business imo."

Mugalli argued that investors were focusing too heavily on near-term weakness while overlooking the company's longer-term opportunities.

"We think the market is punishing the right problem with the wrong time horizon. PCs will recover. Data center growing 78% and a foundry growing 58% are the future of this company. A 20% drop in prices is the bad news. It doesn't price in the turnaround," he said, maintaining an Overweight rating and a $130 price target.
